summary: We are testing whether a multi-heuristic greedy 2D bin packing algorithm (maximal-rectangles + skyline) with randomized search over item orderings can achieve a high score (target ≥80/100) on the Frontier-CS problem #47, a 2D rectangular knapsack with optional 90° rotations, partial credit scoring, and a 1-second time limit across 15 test cases.
key_points: Single experiment arm replaces the empty stub (score 0) with a C++17 solution implementing two complementary packing strategies: maximal-rectangles (BSSF/BAF/BL placement rules) and skyline bottom-left, each tried with multiple deterministic item orderings (by value density, area, height, width) plus randomized density-weighted permutations within 75% of the 1s time budget.

The hypothesis predicts a score ≥80 based on the mechanism that greedily packing high-value-density items into best-fit free rectangles, across diverse orderings, should approximate near-optimal profit. The score is averaged across 15 tests as clamp((V−B)/(K−B), 0, 1) where B is a baseline shelf heuristic and K is a fractional upper bound.

Confirmation: measured judge score ≥80. Partial confirmation: score 50–79 (algorithm works but needs refinement). Refutation: score <50, suggesting greedy multi-heuristic isn't sufficient and more sophisticated methods (e.g., column generation, LP relaxation-guided search, or recursive guillotine cuts) are needed. Key diagnostics if low: check for TLE on large inputs (bins up to 2000×2000 with up to 2000 copies per type), JSON format mismatches, or excessive free-rectangle fragmentation causing quadratic slowdown.
